themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions complaints surged to 75 this week versus a 20.5-week average—a 266% spike (z-score: 6.4)—suggesting rapid pavement or pothole issues emerging across Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights this week that warrant urgent investigation into whether this reflects a discrete incident (storm damage, construction) or systemic maintenance failure.
evidence: 75 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 20.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (266% increase)
Community board has filed recurring 'Other transportation infrastructure requests' suggesting chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Did a specific storm, construction project, or DOT policy change trigger this spike?
Interview residents and business owners about which streets are most affected and impact on mobility/safety

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs Safety Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints exploded to 6 this week from a 0.9-week baseline—a 586% spike (z-score: 6.57)—indicating a sudden cluster of dangling or unstable signage across the district that poses public safety risks and warrants immediate DOT documentation.
evidence: 6 dangling street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (586% spike, z-score: 6.57)
Highest z-score among all spikes, indicating most anomalous outbreak
reporting_angles: Map the specific locations of dangling signs; are they concentrated in one area (wind damage, poor installation)?
Contact DOT about repair timeline and whether budget/staffing shortages explain delayed maintenance

themes_detail.label: Illegal Postings Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 3 two weeks ago from a 0.2-week average—a 1100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting either organized poster activity, lack of enforcement, or both emerging in the district over the past two weeks.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Suggests organized or sudden poster activity not typical in baseline period
reporting_angles: Are postings advertising specific events, illegal services, or political campaigns? Document with photos.
Interview Parks/Sanitation about enforcement frequency and why complaints spiked—understaffing or enforcement gap?

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints jumped to 12 last week from a 2.0-week average—a 500% spike (z-score: 5.0)—indicating a sudden clustering of abandoned cars across the district that may reflect parking enforcement lapses or a specific incident.
evidence: 12 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Overlaps with chronically high illegal parking baseline (6,217 complaints over 90 days), suggesting enforcement infrastructure strain
May block emergency vehicle access or indicate organized chop-shop activity
reporting_angles: Map where derelict vehicles are concentrated; are they near known chop-shop hotspots or in low-enforcement zones?
Interview NYPD and DSNY about removal timeline and whether staffing/towing capacity limits response speed

themes_detail.label: Damaged Trees and Storm Debris
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints surged to 11 this week from a 2.0-week average—a 450% spike (z-score: 5.69)—suggesting either weather damage, disease, or inadequate Parks Department maintenance emerging this week across the district.
evidence: 11 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (450% spike, z-score: 5.69)
Community board repeatedly requests 'New equipment for maintenance' from Parks Department, indicating resource gaps
Damage may be acute (weather) or chronic (deferred maintenance)
reporting_angles: Was there a specific weather event (wind, ice) or pest outbreak causing the spike?
Interview Parks about tree inspection cycles and whether budget constraints delay pruning/removal—tie to recurring budget requests
